docs.summary: Represents event data for pointer-based UI events, providing the source element, its layout rectangle, and pointer positions in multiple coordinate spaces.

members.name: Source
members.signature: public ElementHandle Source { get; internal set; }

docs.summary: The element that triggered the event.

members.name: ElementRect
members.signature: public Rect ElementRect { get; internal set; }

docs.summary: The calculated layout rectangle of the element.
Gets the raw pointer position in screen coordinates.

The pointer in the element's own layout space, the space [`ElementRect`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Events.ElementEvent~ElementRect) is in. The same as [`PointerPosition`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Events.ElementEvent~PointerPosition) unless the element or an ancestor is transformed, and then this is the one to compare against the rectangle.

members.name: NormalizedPosition
members.signature: public Float2 NormalizedPosition { get; internal set; }

docs.summary: The pointer position normalized to the element (0,0 = top-left, 1,1 = bottom-right).

members.name: RelativePosition
members.signature: public Float2 RelativePosition { get; internal set; }

docs.summary: The pointer position relative to the element's top-left corner
Whether propagation has been stopped for this event. When true, the event will not bubble to parent elements.

Stops this event from propagating (bubbling) to parent elements. Similar to DOM's Event.stopPropagation(). This only affects the current event — other event types on the same element are not affected.

members.name: ElementEvent
members.signature: public ElementEvent(ElementHandle source, Rect elementRect, Float2 pointerPos)

docs.summary: Initializes a new event with the given source element, its layout rectangle, and the raw pointer position on screen. Relative and normalized positions are computed automatically.
A screen point in the source element's layout space.

Where [`ElementRect`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.Events.ElementEvent~ElementRect) is drawn on screen, the box around its transformed corners. Anything placed beside the element from outside it, like a popover, anchors to this.
A screen distance in the source element's layout space: a drag of 20 pixels across an element scaled by 2 covers 10 of its own units.
